description: Test whether evidence-linked, object-centric costing provides measurable advantages over strong current alternatives. Treat novelty and frontier claims as empirical questions.
external_dependencies: Independent reference/calculation reviewers and authorised programme-data owners: external validation cannot be inferred from agent-generated fixtures.
edithatogo/voiage, edithatogo/innovate, edithatogo/paignia and process providers: each experiment requires the exact qualified capability it uses.
completion_evidence: Comparators are selected from a dated review and use equivalent inputs, methods and declared capabilities.
Controlled omissions, double counts, unit/date changes and unsupported assumptions have independent expected outcomes.
Incremental revaluation is identical to full recomputation under the agreed exact contract before speed improvements are reported.
Process benchmarks preserve many-to-many objects and compare allocation/denominator errors as well as runtime.
Measurement-planning and capacity experiments use qualified decision/provider contracts and distinguish epistemic uncertainty, heterogeneity and transfers.
External validation reports transportability, missingness, model limitations and analyst effort; synthetic success is not described as empirical programme validation.
Any privacy-preserving or federated experiment measures disclosure risk and utility rather than merely asserting privacy.
